Eco3 designed a community-based research plan, hired and trained canvassers to conduct on-the- ground research integrated into the community-based minimum resilience standards, and assisted in the development of the planning toolkit. Jodi Slick, Founder and CEO: Jodi Slick served as co-PI throughout project conceptualization, application, design, and implementation. Slick coordinated the bottom-up planning approach and community-based participatory research. She led the Community Stakeholder Group and participated as a member of the Critical Infrastructure Team. Slick led development of the minimum resilience standards and is the primary author of the Final Technical Report. Reese Van Houten, Community Resilience and Communications Specialist: Reese Van Houten served as the community-based participatory researcher, conducting focus groups and designing project surveys. Adam Kurowski, Community Projects Manager: Adam Kurowski served on the Critical Infrastructure Team and assisted in prioritizing sites for technical and economic analysis. Helen Davis and Toussaint Stewart, Community Outreach Specialists: Both assisted in survey research and neighborhood outreach strategies focused on oversampling disaster vulnerable populations. 26 Community Outreach Specialist Helen Davis surveys community member to better understand impacts of previous grid outages and preparedness actions taken. (Photo Credit: Reese Van Houten, Ecolibrium3) Collaborating Organizations, Teams, and Stakeholders In addition to the co-led organizations, the City of Duluth and Ecolibrium3, project contributions included LHB Inc, the engineering firm selected to conduct technical and economic analyses of the priority sites identified by the Critical Infrastructure and Community Stakeholder Teams; Grid Catalyst an energy technology incubation firm that assisted with identifying existing and emerging energy technologies that could meet functional needs identified during the project; the University of Duluth Minnesota whose economics faculty member Dr. Neil Wilmot, and social science faculty Dr. Aparna Katre, contributed to project design. The Critical Infrastructure Team (CIT) included Duluth’s electric investor-owned utility (IOU), MN Power and municipal gas utility ComfortSysems, in addition to Duluth Public Works and Utilities, Resource Renew (formerly the Western Lake Superior Sanitary District), St. Louis County Emergency Management, Duluth Fire Department/Emergency Management, Minnesota Department of Homeland Security and Emergency Management, and Ecolibrium3. The CIT outlined outage scenarios, identified components for the site selection rubric, advised on the planning scenarios, and provided valuable input into the toolkit and final resilience plan approaches. The Community Stakeholder Group included representatives from the Ready North Network- multi-stakeholder group established after 2012 flooding in northeastern Minnesota, the Duluth Climate and Energy Network- community and environmental leaders overseeing energy and climate approaches in Duluth, Duluth YMCA- primary health and wellness organization in the region, Northland Chapter of the American Red Cross, Head of the Lakes United Way, Lighthouse Center for Vital Living- focused on older and disabled communities members that need adaptive devices and support for independent living, Duluth Age Friendly Initiative- umbrella partnership addressing community design to ensure all ages can thrive with a subfocus on resilience, Duluth Chamber of Commerce, and City of Duluth. Three communities also aided the project by providing valuable insight into the planning methodologies and toolkit. Participating communities included Moorhead, MN, Maplewood, MN, and Rapid City, SD. 27
